newsitem.title: USA: NCR up slightly on debut day.
newsitem.headline: NCR up slightly on debut day.

text.p: NCR Corp had a solid start to its debut on the New York Stock Exchange, adding 1/4 to 33-5/8 in volume of just over one million shares at 1615 GMT/1115 EST, but analysts say the company has yet to be tested.
The key hurdle will be the attitude of shareholders who received NCR stock as part of its spinoff from AT&T Corp, which was completed on December 31.

"I don't think there will be much analyst coverage, so there is a temptation to sell it because it will be hard to track," said Robert Wilkes of Brown Brothers Harriman, one of only two analysts who have so far issued research on NCR.
The company is not only untested in the stock market, but its independent management and computer market prowess will be hard to judge because of the major cutback in NCR activities in the last year.
"It is still very immature in its current form," said a source at another brokerage which is planning to begin coverage. "We don't think it is a great play," he added.

Wilkes was more optimistic. "The key going forward is whether they can generate sales. It is on a very cheap price to sales ratio for a high technology stock, though it is expensive on its earnings record," he said.
NCR was bought by AT&T in 1991 for $7.5 billion, however it has lost money fairly consistently since.
AT&T brought in Lars Nyberg as chief executive in June 1995 and he drastically cut NCR's jobs and activities, resulting in a $1.6 billion charge to the parent firm in 1995's third quarter.
The stiff medicine has worked to the extent that NCR made a $3 million operating profit in the first nine months of 1996, compared with a $722 million loss in 1995.
But making the slimmed down NCR a market winner is something else, analysts say. -- Nick Louth, New York newsroom 212 859 1610
